name: Salafi jihadism
summary: Salafi jihadism combines the Salafi insistence on God's sole sovereignty and the creed of the early generations with the doctrine that armed jihad is a personal duty. It rejects democracy, nationalism, secularism and man-made law as unbelief, declares rulers who do not govern by sharia apostates, and seeks a caliphate uniting Muslims across borders. Its main strands, al-Qaeda and the Islamic State, differ on whom to fight first and on takfir of other Muslims.
scope: The global jihadi current of Abdullah Azzam, Osama bin Laden's al-Qaeda, Abu Muhammad al-Maqdisi and the Islamic State of Iraq and its successor, as set out in their own statements (1979-2014) and in West Point and Brookings scholarship on them. Where al-Qaeda and the Islamic State diverge (killing of other Muslims, Shia takfir) the answers are left null. It excludes quietist and political Salafism, and nationalist resistance groups. The older entry 'Jihadism' (audits/profiles/jihadism.json) covers the same mainstream; the maintainer should decide whether the two are one ideology.
